The test image shows an opened soybean pod with 3 seeds. One seed (rightmost) has a very prominent **purple/violet stain around the hilum area**. Two other seeds appear cream/yellow and normal. There's some white material visible around the seeds.

Key observations:
- Purple/violet pigmentation extending from/around the hilum of one seed
- Seeds appear plump (not shriveled)
- Pod interior shows some browning

Top candidates: **Purple_Seed_Stain**, Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus, Phomopsis, White_Mold

Let me view reference images to confirm.

The match is definitive. The **Purple_Seed_Stain** reference collage (bottom-right panel) shows an **identical presentation**: an opened soybean pod with one seed displaying a prominent purple/violet stain around the hilum — exactly matching the test image.

- Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus: shows leaf mottling and dark/black seeds — no match
- Phomopsis: shows shriveled/cracked pods with external circular lesions — no match  
- White_Mold: shows white cottony fungal growth on stems — no match

The purple pigment stain concentrated at/around the hilum of one seed while adjacent seeds remain cream/normal is the hallmark of Purple_Seed_Stain (caused by *Cercospora kikuchii*).
